documents.title: Privacy-Preserving Important Passage Retrieval
documents.snippet: State-of-the-art important passage retrieval methods obtain very good results, but do not take into account privacy issues. In this paper, we present a privacy preserving method that relies on creating secure representations of documents. Our approach allows for third parties to retrieve important passages from documents without learning anything regarding their content. grounding_report.query: Synthesize arXiv and Crossref studies comparing dense passage retrieval versus sparse SPLADE expansion on BEIR.
grounding_report.final_answer:
Query Expansion Should Be Coordinated: Dense Expands, Sparse Anchors: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems rely on retrieval modules to ground large language model (LLM) outputs. LLM-based query expansion enriches retrieval with document-like passages, but evaluations of hybrid retrieval often fuse fixed top-L prefixes of dense and sparse rankings. Because L controls cross-channel contributions and ranking access, it can alter measured expansion gains. We therefore evaluate complete-list effectiveness and record per-channel replay stopping depths required.
Mistral-SPLADE: LLMs for better Learned Sparse Retrieval: Learned Sparse Retrievers (LSR) have evolved into an effective retrieval strategy that can bridge the gap between traditional keyword-based sparse retrievers and embedding-based dense retrievers. At its core, learned sparse retrievers try to learn the most important semantic keyword expansions from a query and/or document which can facilitate better retrieval with overlapping keyword expansions. LSR like SPLADE has typically been using encoder only models with MLM (masked language modeling) styl.
Hybrid Dense-Sparse Retrieval for High-Recall Information Retrieval: . DOI: 10.2139/ssrn.6013934.
Optimizing Approximate Nearest Neighbour-Based Dense Retrieval for Efficient Passage Ranking with Query Expansion: International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems. DOI: 10.22266/ijies2025.0831.45.

documents.title: Query Expansion Should Be Coordinated: Dense Expands, Sparse Anchors
documents.snippet: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems rely on retrieval modules to ground large language model (LLM) outputs. LLM-based query expansion enriches retrieval with document-like passages, but evaluations of hybrid retrieval often fuse fixed top-L prefixes of dense and sparse rankings. Because L controls cross-channel contributions and ranking access, it can alter measured expansion gains. We therefore evaluate complete-list effectiveness and record per-channel replay stopping depths required
documents.citation: Query Expansion Should Be Coordinated: Dense Expands, Sparse Anchors (arXiv, 2026). http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15851v2

documents.title: Mistral-SPLADE: LLMs for better Learned Sparse Retrieval
documents.snippet: Learned Sparse Retrievers (LSR) have evolved into an effective retrieval strategy that can bridge the gap between traditional keyword-based sparse retrievers and embedding-based dense retrievers. At its core, learned sparse retrievers try to learn the most important semantic keyword expansions from a query and/or document which can facilitate better retrieval with overlapping keyword expansions. LSR like SPLADE has typically been using encoder only models with MLM (masked language modeling) styl
documents.citation: Mistral-SPLADE: LLMs for better Learned Sparse Retrieval (arXiv, 2024). http://arxiv.org/abs/2408.11119v2

documents.title: Query Expansion Should Be Coordinated: Dense Expands, Sparse Anchors
documents.snippet: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems rely on retrieval modules to ground large language model (LLM) outputs. LLM-based query expansion enriches retrieval with document-like passages, but evaluations of hybrid retrieval often fuse fixed top-L prefixes of dense and sparse rankings. Because L controls cross-channel contributions and ranking access, it can alter measured expansion gains. We therefore evaluate complete-list effectiveness and record per-channel replay stopping depths required

documents.title: Mistral-SPLADE: LLMs for better Learned Sparse Retrieval
documents.snippet: Learned Sparse Retrievers (LSR) have evolved into an effective retrieval strategy that can bridge the gap between traditional keyword-based sparse retrievers and embedding-based dense retrievers. At its core, learned sparse retrievers try to learn the most important semantic keyword expansions from a query and/or document which can facilitate better retrieval with overlapping keyword expansions. LSR like SPLADE has typically been using encoder only models with MLM (masked language modeling) styl
